title: Domain-neutral structured research claim schema v0
problem: Current claim fields capture a proposition and quote but not enough scientific context to distinguish an observed result from a method, cited background statement, or speculation. Structured metadata is required for semantic validation and useful retrieval.
acceptance_criteria: The core claim contract can represent claim_kind, study_design, population_or_sample, intervention_or_exposure, comparator, outcome, effect_direction, statistical_context, limitations, and section provenance without creativity-specific fields.
Requiredness is conditional and deterministic: empirical-result claims require outcome and section provenance; non-empirical claims are not forced into an empirical schema.
Unknown or absent fields are explicit and never fabricated from defaults.
Candidate JSON validation rejects invalid enum values, contradictory field combinations, and section provenance that does not match the source chunk.
Existing mock fixtures either migrate explicitly or remain supported through a versioned backward-compatibility path; no silent field invention is allowed.
Database migration and serialization tests prove private structured metadata does not widen public exports.
On completion, ticket-417 changes from blocked to ready; no later Phase 4 ticket is activated.
test_plan: With mock-only env: python -m pytest tests/golden -q
With mock-only env: python -m rge.cli verify --skip-site
non_goals: Do not require all claim types to contain statistical fields.
Do not encode creativity ontology fields in the core schema.
Do not add semantic model review or human review UI.
Do not expose private scientific metadata through public cards without a later explicit ticket.
rollback_plan: Revert structured-field consumers and retain backward-readable nullable migration columns if applied. Restore the prior claim schema version without deleting existing claim data.
